issuer: Shoreline Regional Medical Center / Bay City Medical Center
text: Shoreline Regional Medical Center and Bay City Medical Center today released their joint Hurricane Rafael Hospital Operations After-Action Report. The report documents the response of both facilities from September 11 through October 14, 2027. Combined, the two hospitals treated 4,217 hurricane-related patients over that period. The response involved two distinct patient surge waves: a trauma wave from landfall on September 14 through September 21, during which SRMC operated at up to 140% licensed bed capacity on generator power, and a waterborne disease cluster from September 29 through October 12, during which 1,820 patients were treated for Cryptosporidium and Giardia infection. The cluster was geographically concentrated in Water Districts 3 and 4. The report notes that early-cluster admissions disproportionately included patients from Spanish-dominant households, a pattern the report identifies as potentially related to the delay in Spanish-language boil-water notification. No patient deaths were directly attributable to the hospital surge response. The report recommends expanded generator diesel reserves, pre-positioned water testing capabilities, and enhanced multilingual patient communication protocols for future mass casualty and public health emergency events.

issuer: Texas Commission on Environmental Quality / EPA Region 6
text: 60-DAY REMEDIATION ASSESSMENT — November 13, 2027: The Texas Commission on Environmental Quality and EPA Region 6 have completed the 60-day remediation assessment for the Inner Harbor oil release (TCEQ Incident Case CC-ENV-2027-0916). Water quality monitoring shows Corpus Christi Bay total petroleum hydrocarbon concentrations have returned to 0.03 mg/L, below the TCEQ Class 2 surface water standard of 0.05 mg/L. Nueces Bay shoreline cleanup is 94 percent complete; minor tar ball accumulation persists on approximately 0.4 kilometers of shoreline near the Nueces Bay Causeway and will be addressed through the 2028 spring shoreline maintenance program. Raw-water intake readings at the O.N. Stevens Water Treatment Plant have remained below the hydrocarbon alert threshold for 52 consecutive days. The emergency response phase is hereby closed. Fishing and shellfish harvesting closures remain in effect until state testing supports reopening. Long-term ecological monitoring of Nueces Bay seagrass beds and oyster reef habitats will continue under a separate TCEQ Natural Resource Damage Assessment agreement with the owners of MT Kalvora Star and MT Ostrel Bay Total documented cleanup cost is $8.2 million. Wildlife rehabilitation costs of $0.9 million and estimated commercial fishing economic losses of $5.6 million are subject to Natural Resource Damage Assessment proceedings. This assessment has been transmitted to NOAA, USFWS, and Texas Parks and Wildlife for NRD purposes.
